screens.title: About you
screens.prompt: Create ONE separate portrait Android app screen concept for Lockout's new required first-launch profile onboarding. This is a visual approval mockup, not shipping code. Full-screen native mobile UI only, no device frame, no Android status or system gesture bar, no bottom app tabs. Portrait canvas. Faithfully extend the approved Material 3 Expressive app: pale green-white surface, Rep lime #C2EE7B primary containers, dark olive ink #1F2E00 primary text/buttons, soft mint secondary and pale aqua tertiary containers; flat colors, no gradients, glass or shadows. Bricolage Grotesque-like confident display headings, Figtree-like readable body. Strong 32sp heading hierarchy and 16sp body, generous 20dp margins, 48dp minimum touch targets. Distinct lobed/rounded Material-shaped icon badges, but text and forms stay rounded rectangles. Filled form controls with small labels INSIDE the top of the filled surface, values below; NEVER labels straddling the outside border. Consistent top brand row: tiny upward-angled dumbbell logo and 'Lockout', step count on right; underneath a 5-segment rounded progress indicator. All copy sentence case. Fixed bottom primary pill button with safe content spacing, secondary Back where applicable. No Skip action. Sample filled values illustrate user-entered inputs, never automatic defaults. No decorative photos or illustrations. Make this look like a polished real Android Material 3 Expressive setup, not a website. Screen 1 of 5, 'About you'. One dark-olive user-outline icon in a lime expressive flower badge above a large heading 'Make it yours'. Supporting copy 'A few details to build your starting plan. Everything stays on your device.' Filled 'Age (years)' numeric field showing 30. Below, label 'Sex for calorie estimates', two broad expressive connected selectable buttons 'Male' (selected lime) and 'Female' (unselected pale mint). Small readable explanation 'Used by the calorie equation. You can edit this later.' Spacious composition with no extra fields. Bottom full-width primary button 'Continue'; below it a tonal outlined/text action 'Restore backup'. Top step count '1 of 5'. Design should feel welcoming but focused on actual input, not a marketing slide.
